matches.quote: Calling the illumination-induced T_c drop "counterintuitive" presupposes a density-controlled T_c that the authors' own Introduction contradicts.
The key statement that "superconductivity and PNR alignment are strengthened by gate cycling and suppressed by illumination" is asserted rather than measured.
Plot T_c against μ, R_s, n and k_F·l for all gate-cycled and illuminated states together.
add a direct polarization probe (low-T SHG, PFM through thin AlOₓ, or remnant-polarization/pyroelectric current) and an OV charge-state probe
All data appear to come from one sample. Sample-to-sample reproducibility, dependence on AlOₓ thickness or reduction conditions... are absent.
If T_c vs. μ (or vs. R_s, k_F·l) collapses onto a single curve for both gate-cycled and illuminated states, the PNR-mediated pairing picture is unnecessary.
Sample-to-sample reproducibility, dependence on AlOₓ thickness or reduction conditions, and comparison with other orientations or capping layers are absent.
The temperature dependence of relaxation magnitude and kinetics may therefore partly reflect varying illumination dose and LED heating (visible at 2 K in Fig. 2b).
The identification of a "deviation" at 35 K and an "onset" at 95 K depends on a handful of points, where Δ_L ≈ 0 near 95 K.
If T_c vs. μ (or vs. R_s, k_F·l) collapses onto a single curve for both gate-cycled and illuminated states, the PNR-mediated pairing picture is unnecessary.
Add perpendicular/parallel H_c2 data, from which coherence length and possible changes in 2D thickness can be extracted.
Correlate the kinetics with the dielectric relaxation times τ = 1/ω(T) extracted from Fig. 3c, so that common microscopic timescales are compared quantitatively
Quantify retention time, number of write/erase cycles and dose (photon fluence) dependence
The Arrhenius fits (Fig. 3c) lack uncertainties for T_p, E_a and the attempt frequencies.
The manuscript never shows that illumination returns T_c (or R_s at the same temperature) to the pristine, pre-gating value.
Quantify retention time, number of write/erase cycles and dose (photon fluence) dependence with a calibrated, temperature-independent light source
the analysis also neglects the finite 2DEG sheet resistance (~800 Ω) and the wiring.

notes: C1 and C25 are judged partly raised via P20 (and P14/P10), which argues that mobility/disorder scaling from defect trapping/PPC explains the transport and Tc trends without PNR-mediated pairing. C2 is partly raised via P11, P2, and P15 (measuring retention/hold-time decay and quantitatively comparing transport relaxation times to the Arrhenius dielectric timescales). C20 (gate leakage as device quality issue in Supp. Fig. 3) and C16 (simulating PNR internal gating potential) are only tangentially touched on by P12 and P9, so they are strictly marked not raised.
